overview: This table sets the rank tiers players see, the point ranges that unlock them, and how much a loss can cost.
description: One row defines a rank tier: it joins a GlobalThresholdDataTable point band to the rank class/grade shown in UI, used by lobby/session rules, ranked rewards and KPI, and it supplies that tier's floor for a non-draw loss.

Id.simple: The name of this rank tier, such as Grade 4 or Special Grade. The game uses this name to tell ranks apart and find this tier.
Id.technical: FName import key/row name for FGameDataTableRow_RankPoint; the export writes the key as "ID" while ImportKeyField is Id. GameRankPoint_FindRow does not read Id: it enumerates cached rows via FGameDataTableArray::GetRows (table order, then each table's GetRowNames order) and selects by threshold. The previous/next UI helpers instead sort rows by the Min of their Id_GlobalThreshold thresholds and locate the current row with Row->Id == Current->Id. Result UI compares CurrentRank->Id with PreviousRank->Id only to detect no change; if the Ids differ, CurrentPoint <= PreviousPoint selects down and otherwise up. Leaderboard card packing maps the found row's Id to a 0..63 index stored in 10 bits; unpacking indexes the same row list to recover the tier's threshold Min. Shop unlock text and PvPRankPointMax gating find rows directly by a configured row name (ValueStrs[0]) with the shared StoryFindRowOutOfLine finder (bCheckNone=false).

RankPointClass.simple: The main rank group players see on their rank display, from Grade 4 up to Special Grade. Moving it up raises the shown rank and changes matchmaking and ranked match rewards.
RankPointClass.technical: EGameRankPointClass is a uint8 enum (None=0, Grade4=1, Grade3=2, SemiGrade2=3, Grade2=4, SemiGrade1=5, Grade1=6, SpecialGrade=7, Max=8, Invalid=255); constructor default None, and all 27 exported rows use 1..7. SetRank is called from UGamePlayerRankWidget::SetRankPoint and GameRankSystemGradeInfoWidget::SetupGradeInfo: it selects the class icon through AGameWidgetManager::GetRankPointClassIconTexture and shows only the matching grade spacer (spacers registered for Grade4, Grade3, SemiGrade2, Grade2, SemiGrade1 and Grade1; SpecialGrade collapses them all). Result, ranking, replay and shop UI use the numeric value as GSysRankingLabelMap key for localized grade names; the PvE result path uses the same values in GPvPRankMatchRewardLobbyLabelMap / GPvPRankMatchRewardLabelMap to grant an item set. Session helpers map Grade4/Grade3 to a None border, SemiGrade2 to Grade4, Grade2 to Grade3, SemiGrade1 to SemiGrade2 and Grade1/SpecialGrade to Grade2, then advertise/query point borders from GGameRankPointClassBorders (None 1200, Grade4 1300, Grade3 1500, SemiGrade2 1600, Grade2 1700, SemiGrade1 5000); GetRankBorderClass adds an optional class delta, clamping it to 0..4 only when the delta is nonzero. Lobby join/create checks the player's class against session minimum/maximum. Battle KPI rows store the numeric class as a string (0 when no row is found).

RankPointGrade.simple: The small rank marks shown inside a rank group, with Vermilion and Special Grade showing none. Moving this up adds marks from Bronze to Platinum.
RankPointGrade.technical: EGameRankPointGrade is a uint8 enum (None=0, Vermilion=1, Bronze=2, Silver=3, Gold=4, Platinum=5, Invalid=255); constructor default None. The export uses Vermilion/Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum on the 26 classed rows and None on SPECIAL_GRADE_01. SetRank passes it to UGamePlayerRankGradeWidget::SetGrade, which shows each mark when Grade >= its key for Bronze=2, Silver=3, Gold=4 and Platinum=5, so Vermilion and None display no marks. The rank-system manual filters rows to the selected RankPointClass, stable-sorts them descending by RankPointGrade (Platinum first, Vermilion last) and feeds up to five GradeInfoWidgets; each displays the row's threshold Min/Max plus previous/next progress. Battle KPI rows also record the numeric grade (0 when no row is found).

Id_GlobalThreshold.simple: The name of the point range that decides when this rank appears. Changing it connects this tier to a different range of rank points.
Id_GlobalThreshold.technical: FName, default None, pointing into GlobalThresholdDataTable (DTM+0x300); the referenced row supplies float Min/Max (both default 0). GameRankPoint_FindRow (0x13077a0) enumerates RankPointDataTables (DTM+0x380) through FGameDataTableArray::GetRows and calls the per-table FindRow helper with bCheckNone=false for each Id_GlobalThreshold. It keeps the first row seen as a fallback, and returns a row immediately when UKismetMathLibrary::InRange_FloatFloat(static_cast<float>(RankPoint), Threshold->Min, Threshold->Max, true, true) succeeds: both float bounds are inclusive, a row whose threshold is missing is skipped, and if no rows exist the result is null rather than a synthetic default. All 27 exported keys resolve to distinct threshold rows with contiguous, non-overlapping bands covering 0..99999. UI helpers sort rows by WidgetTest_FindGlobalThreshold(...)->Min; grade-info displays Min/Max and uses previous/next row Mins for progress, with 'next' limited to rows of the same RankPointClass. Result UI uses the next row's Min for progress/remaining points (or a full bar when there is no next row); the shop PvPRankPointMax unlock compares the saved record with ceil(Threshold->Min). Leaderboard card unpacking converts the stored row index back to round(Threshold->Min), returning 0 past the end of the row list.

LoseLowerLimit.simple: The smallest rank-point drop after a non-draw ranked loss, with values closer to zero meaning a gentler drop. An AI-controlled ally can stop the drop completely.
LoseLowerLimit.technical: int32 floor in rank-point units, constructor default 0. At the end of CalcRankPointDelta, after result base, evaluation, stock difference and optional rank-gap scaling, it is read only when the winner is not the 0xFF draw sentinel and the player's team lost: Points = FMath::Max(Points, Row->LoseLowerLimit), where Row is found for the pre-battle GameManager UserInfo.Header.RankPoint. A null finder result skips the floor. If any ally with a valid online-user index has GetControlType()==3 (AI control), a second FMath::Max(Points, 0) applies. Draws instead clamp to <= 0 and never read this field; wins do not read it. Exported floors are 0 for the six Grade4/Grade3 rows, -5 SemiGrade2, -10 Grade2, -20 SemiGrade1, -22/-24/-26/-28/-30 for Grade1 rows 1..5, and -40 SpecialGrade. The resulting delta is applied by AddRankPoint, which clamps saved rank points to [0, 99999].

notes: Export/cache scope: one RankPointDataTable object (RowStruct GameDataTableRow_RankPoint, ImportKeyField Id) with 27 rows; the site catalog has one variant and the exports/project Content contain no localized or numbered RankPointDataTable shards. RankPointCalculationDataTable is a distinct table with its own row struct, not a shard, but CalcRankPointDelta reads LoseLowerLimit through this table.

Load path: StartInitialLoading registers the RankPointDataTable primary asset name; once loading completes, AGameDataTableManager::Tick resolves it and AddLoadedDataTables appends only non-null UDataTable pointers to RankPointDataTables (DTM+0x380). Row order is table order then each table's GetRowNames order; it is not re-sorted by the finder.

Fallback and null handling: with at least one row, an unmatched or missing threshold leaves the first enumerated row as GameRankPoint_FindRow's result. With no rows at all it returns nullptr. Some consumers dereference unconditionally (UGamePlayerRankWidget::SetRankPoint, result-change UI, lobby create/join, replay card), while others guard it (online KPI, session border helpers, ranked-match reward path, rank-manual open).

Data relationships: all 27 Id_GlobalThreshold keys resolve to unique global-threshold rows whose inclusive bands are contiguous from 0 through 99999; SPECIAL_GRADE_01 covers 7600..99999 and is the only row with grade None. Class values 1..7 are used directly as map keys for rank labels, reward item sets and border tables; grade values 2..5 drive grade-mark visibility. None=0 and Invalid=255 are enum sentinels absent from the export; the session -1 RankPoint parameter means 'any rank' and bypasses the finder.

Reconstruction status: status/functions.json marks finder 0x13077a0 as byte MATCH (550 B, verdict from Tools/verify/LANES/w22-story-a.md:35, matched RVA 0x1c88260), next-row helper 0x1626350 as behavioural/certified (RB1F.json; verdicts.json records 169 unmasked diffs and +2 B), grade-info setup 0x1639900 as behavioural/certified (T05.json), and result-change SetRankChangePoint 0x163c710 as byte MATCH. Details here describe reconstructed C++ behaviour plus static export evidence; no retail Blueprint graphs, live game run or original retail DataTable asset were inspected, so editor-only/Blueprint consumers cannot be excluded.

usages.detail: Resolves the loaded RankPointDataTable asset into RankPointDataTables (DTM+0x380); null tables are filtered by AddLoadedDataTables.
GameRankPoint_FindRow maps a numeric rank point to a tier through Id_GlobalThreshold; SetRankPoint feeds the row's class/grade to the rank widget.
CalcRankPointDelta floors a non-draw loss with the found row's LoseLowerLimit, then optionally raises it to >= 0 for an AI ally.
Shows class/grade plus threshold Min/Max and previous/next progress; the next row is only used when it shares the same RankPointClass.
Filters rows by selected RankPointClass, sorts descending by RankPointGrade and distributes them across the grade-info widgets.
Result count-up maps class to a localized label and threshold progress, and uses row Id equality plus point direction for rank-up/down animations.
Session advertise/search maps RankPointClass to fixed point borders and sorts results by them; RankPoint == -1 skips the rank constraint.
Ranked-match reward selection finds the pre-battle rank row and maps its RankPointClass to an item-set reward for normal and lobby modes.
Packs a leaderboard card with the rank row's 6-bit row index and reconstructs a point value from that row's threshold Min on unpack.
PvPRankPointMax shop unlock resolves a configured RankPoint row by name and tests the saved record against ceil(its threshold Min).
PvP battle KPI rows record the numeric rank class and grade from the found row.
Lobby join and creation compare the player's rank class with session rank limits and write the class into create-session settings.
